patterns: Row types inherit EntityRow base: {id, user_id, field_hlcs: Record<string, string>, deleted_at: string | null, created_at: string, updated_at: string, ...domain-specific fields}
Dexie indices via .stores(): Primary key 'id', secondary indexes on 'user_id', 'updated_at', or compound [user_id+field] for multi-key queries
Version bumps: Dexie.version(N).stores({new_table: '...'}) for EACH new table, cumulative not replacement. Compare with previous migration.
Operations: generateOp({entity_kind, entity_id, op_type: 'create'|'update'|'delete', payload: Record<string, unknown>, user_id}) → Op. Payload only includes fields being set.

Server materialization: For each entity_kind, export const XYZ_FIELDS = [...field names...] from entity-fields.ts; case in materializeRow() calls materializeRow_LWW(db, op, userId, 'table_name', XYZ_FIELDS)
Client application: In sync-client.ts applyLocalOp(), add case for new entity_kind that gets current row from db.{table_name}, calls applyOp(), then puts result back

D1 schema: Create table with id PRIMARY KEY, user_id NOT NULL, domain fields, field_hlcs TEXT NOT NULL (JSON), deleted_at TEXT (tombstone), created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT. Add indexes on user_id and frequently-queried fields.
Hooks query pattern: useLiveQuery(async () => { await db.{table}.where('user_id').equals(userId).toArray() }) then filter deleted_at and apply business logic sort/filter
Field HLCs for per-field LWW: Record<string, hlc_string> tracks each field's last-modified HLC independently. Deletes marked via deleted_at field with its own HLC.
gotchas: ENTITY_KINDS in ops.ts must be updated BEFORE adding a case in sync-client.ts applyLocalOp() — if an unknown entity_kind arrives, it silently falls through (line 102-103 comment shows 'project'/'learning'/'note'/'budget' placeholders)

Dexie version() calls are cumulative: version(2) does NOT replace version(1) stores, it ADDS to them. Each .version(N).stores({...}) only declares NEW/MODIFIED stores for that version. Old stores implicitly carry forward.
field_hlcs must be Record<string, string> in TypeScript but serialized as JSON string in D1 (TEXT column). Parse when reading, stringify when writing. materializeRow_LWW handles this.

deleted_at is both a tombstone marker (field with its own HLC in field_hlcs) AND a nullable column. Set to ISO string on delete, null on undelete (resurrection). Queries must filter deleted_at IS NULL.
Row types exported from dexie.ts but applyOp() in op-log.ts returns generic EntityRow — cast with `as never` in sync-client to satisfy TypeScript when the shape doesn't exactly match yet.
Compound indices in Dexie use [key1+key2] syntax with square brackets; in D1 migrations use UNIQUE or separate indices. Example: Dexie '[user_id+kind]' vs D1 'UNIQUE (user_id, name, kind)'
Materialization is server-only; client Dexie tables are the source of truth. Ops sync bidirectionally but materialized D1 rows are projections used only by cron/digest jobs.

schema_version in Op payload (ops.ts line 15, set to SCHEMA_VERSION=1 in sync-client.ts) must increment if op_type='create' or 'update' changes the schema for an entity_kind. For new domains, start at schema_version 1.

When adding a field to an existing entity (not a new domain), old ops won't include that field in payload, so materializeRow_LWW checks 'merged[f] !== undefined' to avoid explicit NULLs clobbering DB defaults (line 77).
FxRateRow is unique: no user_id, uses compound primary key [date+target], stored as Table<FxRateRow> not EntityTable<>. Don't follow FxRate pattern for domain entities.

dimensionMaps.dimension: sync-oplog: Hybrid Logical Clock + per-field LWW + server materialization via op-log

keyFiles.role: Central type definitions: ENTITY_KINDS array, Op schema, EntityRow type; entity_kind is a Zod enum sourced from this const.
Client sync orchestration: generateOp() creates ops with HLC, applyLocalOp() applies to Dexie with entity_kind switch, pushPullOnce() fetches /api/sync. SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 constant.
Per-field LWW logic: applyOp(existing, op) merges via compareHlc; field only updates if op.hlc > existing.field_hlcs[field]; handles create/update/delete + resurrection.
Server materialization: materializeRow() dispatches by entity_kind to specific or generic LWW upsert; rebinds JSON field_hlcs, applies applyOp, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upserts to D1.
HLC (Hybrid Logical Clock) primitives: createHlc, serializeHlc (format: 16-digit-0-6-digit-0-deviceId), parseHlc, compareHlc, tickHlc, receiveHlc.
Per-entity_kind field lists (MONEY_FIELDS, RECURRING_FIELDS, TASK_FIELDS, CATEGORY_FIELDS, INSIGHT_FIELDS); used by materializeRow_LWW to decide which columns to write.
Client IndexedDB schema via Dexie v4; EntityTable<T, 'id'> for each entity_kind; includes version() blocks with indexes; db.transactions in applyLocalOp touch all tables at once.
Server Kysely<DB> schema types (UserTable, CategoryTable, TaskTable, etc.); mirrors D1 SQL; used in /api/sync and materializeRow.

POST /api/sync endpoint: accepts device_id, last_synced_hlc, new_ops; merges via mergeOpsForUser; inserts to op_log; calls materializeRow; returns server_hlc, new_ops_from_server (> lastSyncedHlc), applied_ack.
POST /api/admin/backfill endpoint: idempotent replay of caller's entire op_log in HLC order; calls materializeRow for each op; used for one-time server materialization after schema migrations.
mergeOpsForUser(existingOps, incomingOps, lastSyncedHlc): deduplicates by op.id, returns newOps and opsForClient (filtered by HLC > lastSyncedHlc).
Phase 0 schema: user, session, account, verification, devices, op_log (PK=id, FK=user_id; CHECK op_type IN), widgets (with field_hlcs JSON, deleted_at tombstone, created_at/updated_at ISO strings).
Phase 1 schema: categories, recurring_rules, money_entries; all with field_hlcs TEXT, deleted_at, created_at/updated_at ISO, user_id FK.
Phase 2 schema: tasks table with title, due_at, priority, completed_at, source, field_hlcs, deleted_at ISO timestamps, indexes on (user_id, due_at) and (user_id, completed_at).

Phase 3 schema: insights table (period, starts_at/ends_at, summary, metrics JSON, field_hlcs, deleted_at, created_at/updated_at), push_subscriptions, push_notifications; added receipt_key to money_entries.

patterns: ENTITY_KINDS: Const array in src/types/ops.ts; must add new entity_kind string here before any use. Example: ENTITY_KINDS = [..., 'note'] as const.
Op flow: generateOp(entity_kind, entity_id, op_type, payload, user_id) → applyLocalOp(op) → pushPullOnce() → /api/sync POST → server merges + materializes.
Client apply: applyLocalOp() switches on entity_kind and db.transaction(['rw', [tables...], async () => { db.op_log.add(op); switch(op.entity_kind) { case 'new': db.tables.put(applyOp(...)) } }])
Server apply: POST /api/sync calls materializeRow(db, op, userId) which switches on entity_kind and upserts to D1 via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT.
Per-field LWW: field_hlcs is JSON Record<string, string> (client) or TEXT (D1); each field carries its own HLC; applyOp only writes field if op.hlc > existing.field_hlcs[field].
HLC serialization: 16-digit physicalMs (padded), 6-digit logical counter, deviceId; lexicographically sortable; tickHlc increments logical if same ms, resets logical if time advances.
Timestamp derivation: hlcToIso(hlc) in applyOp converts HLC.physicalMs to ISO string for created_at/updated_at; deterministic across replicas.
Tombstoning: deleted_at is a special 'field' in field_hlcs; delete op sets field_hlcs.deleted_at = op.hlc; update with later HLC clears tombstone (resurrection).

Optional fields: In materializeRow_LWW, only write merged[f] to row if !== undefined; avoids explicit NULL which bypasses SQL DEFAULT; matches per-field LWW (op never touching field must not clobber it).
D1 table shape: id (PK), user_id (FK + index), field_hlcs (TEXT JSON), deleted_at (ISO tombstone), created_at/updated_at (ISO strings), domain-specific fields, indexes on (user_id, sort_key).
Dexie table shape: EntityTable<T, 'id'> with T extending { field_hlcs: Record<string, string>; deleted_at: string | null; created_at: string; updated_at: string; } + domain fields.
Synchronization checkpoint: lastSyncedHlc tracked in sync_meta; client sends it on POST /api/sync; server returns ops where hlc > lastSyncedHlc; idempotent if same lastSyncedHlc resent.
Schema versioning: schema_version: integer in Op, currently = 1 constant in sync-client.ts; incremented only when Op format itself changes, not per entity_kind.
Materialization idempotency: materializeRow calls applyOp on existing row (if any) then upserts; safe to replay same op multiple times; /api/admin/backfill uses this for one-time recovery.

Entity-fields definition: For each new entity_kind, create const FOO_FIELDS = [...field names...] in entity-fields.ts; passed to materializeRow_LWW to control which columns are written (skip undefined ones).
Device tracking: getDeviceId() generates 12-char hex ID on first call, stores in sync_meta; all ops tagged with this device_id; allows multi-device HLC ordering.
gotchas: field_hlcs mismatch: D1 stores as TEXT with JSON.stringify(), applyOp expects Record<string, string>; materializeRow_LWW does JSON.parse(existing.field_hlcs) on read, JSON.stringify() on write; mismatched types cause silent failures.

Explicit NULL vs undefined: In materializeRow_LWW, if merged[f] === null (user explicitly set to null), it WILL be written to row; but merged[f] === undefined skips the key, allowing SQL DEFAULT or existing value to apply. Ops that never touched a field must send payload with field absent, not payload[field]: null.

Dexie transaction scope: applyLocalOp uses db.transaction('rw', [op_log, widgets, money_entries, recurring_rules, categories, tasks, insights], () => {...}); must add NEW entity table here or applyLocalOp won't touch it. Forgetting this silently skips the update.
applyOp resurrection: if existing.deleted_at is set and op.hlc > field_hlcs.deleted_at, applyOp clears deleted_at; this resurrects tombstoned rows. Don't double-delete if re-applying ops.

HLC overflow: Serialized HLC is padStart(16, '0') for ms and padStart(6, '0') for logical; Year 10000 (ts ~253402300799999) will overflow 16 digits; not a practical concern for ~7980 years but worth noting.

schema_version bump: If Op wire format ever changes (new fields, renamed fields), increment SCHEMA_VERSION in sync-client.ts AND the const in every Op; clients with old version will send ops server won't parse. No auto-versioning migration logic yet.

mergeOpsForUser deduplication: Deduplicates by op.id; if client sends same op.id twice, only first is new, second filtered out. But if server rejects one op and client retries, op.id must stay the same (idempotency key).

lastSyncedHlc comparison: Uses compareHlc(parseHlc(op.hlc), parseHlc(lastSyncedHlc)) > 0; lexicographic sort on serialized string also works but compareHlc is explicit; if lastSyncedHlc is missing, ALL known ops sent to client.

Dexie versioning: Each version() block is additive; when adding a new table, add a new version() block with incremented version number and all prior tables' indexes. Don't reuse an existing version() number.

D1 foreign keys: Categories referenced by money_entries and recurring_rules; if FK referenced table doesn't exist on server at materialize time, SQLITE_CONSTRAINT. Phase 3 backfill relied on HLC ordering to ensure categories materialized before money entries.

Insight metrics JSON: metrics field is TEXT (JSON string) in D1 but InsightRow on client carries it as string too (not deserialized); caller must JSON.parse(metrics) on client; inconsistent with other JSON fields.

Device ID generation: crypto.randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 12); takes first 12 hex chars; collision risk is negligible but not cryptographically unique. Used in HLC serialization so must be stable.

HLC device ordering: compareHlc breaks ties with deviceId < comparison; lexicographically later device_id wins in case of identical physical + logical; not a semantic ordering, just deterministic tiebreaker.

POST /api/sync no transaction: Server loop calls materializeRow in separate upserts, NOT in a transaction; if one fails partway, op_log row inserted but D1 row not. Backfill route should be called after to retry.
Empty op_log: If no ops exist for user, serverHlc defaults to '0000000000000000-000000-server'; if comparing, ensure this string is handled correctly in HLC parsing.

Timezone in timestamps: created_at/updated_at are ISO strings derived from HLC.physicalMs (milliseconds since epoch UTC); they're in UTC regardless of user timezone; user_prefs.tz is separate, not used in sync engine.

Multi-entity transactions: If one entity's op should trigger an operation on another entity, you must generate two ops and apply both locally in same transaction; sync engine has no cross-entity consistency, only per-field LWW.
newDomainSteps: Step 1: Add entity_kind to ENTITY_KINDS const in src/types/ops.ts. Example: export const ENTITY_KINDS = ['widget', 'money', 'recurring', 'task', 'project', 'learning', 'note', 'category', 'budget', 'insight', 'FOO'] as const. This is the source of truth for the Zod enum OpSchema.entity_kind.

Step 2: Define field list in src/lib/entity-fields.ts. Create: export const FOO_FIELDS = ['field1', 'field2', 'field3'] as const. These fields will be the only columns written to D1 during materializeRow_LWW; ensure they match your D1 schema.

Step 3: Create D1 migration file migrations/000N_foo_domain.sql (increment N after highest existing). Include: CREATE TABLE foo (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES user(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, field1 TEXT, field2 TEXT, ... field_hlcs TEXT NOT NULL, deleted_at TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL); CREATE INDEX idx_foo_user ON foo(user_id); add any domain-specific indexes on (user_id, sort_key).

Step 4: Add Dexie table type in src/lib/dexie.ts. Create export type FooRow = { id: string; user_id: string; field1: string; field2?: string; field_hlcs: Record<string, string>; deleted_at: string | null; created_at: string; updated_at: string; }.
Step 5: Add Dexie EntityTable to PulseDb class in src/lib/dexie.ts. Add line: foo!: EntityTable<FooRow, 'id'> after other entity tables.

Step 6: Add Dexie version() block in PulseDb constructor. Add a new this.version(N+1).stores({ foo: 'id, user_id, [user_id+sort_key]' }) after the highest existing version, with appropriate indexes for your queries.

Step 7: Add Kysely table type in src/lib/db.ts. Create interface FooTable { id: string; user_id: string; field1: string; field2: string | null; field_hlcs: string; deleted_at: string | null; created_at: string; updated_at: string; }. Add to DB interface: foo: FooTable.

Step 8: Add case in applyLocalOp switch in src/lib/sync-client.ts. Pattern: case 'foo': { const current = await db.foo.get(op.entity_id); const next = applyOp(current as never, op); await db.foo.put(next as never); return; }

Step 9: Add db.foo to transaction scope in applyLocalOp. Modify line: await db.transaction('rw', [db.op_log, db.widgets, db.money_entries, db.recurring_rules, db.categories, db.tasks, db.insights, db.foo], async () => { ... });

Step 10: Add case in materializeRow switch in src/lib/materialize.ts. If simple LWW: case 'foo': return materializeRow_LWW(db, op, userId, 'foo', FOO_FIELDS). If special logic (like widgets), create materializeFoo function following materializeWidget pattern.
Step 11: Ensure FOO_FIELDS exported from entity-fields.ts and imported at top of materialize.ts. Add: import { MONEY_FIELDS, ..., FOO_FIELDS } from '@/lib/entity-fields'.
Step 12: (Optional) If entity has special creation/application logic, extend op-log.ts applyUpdate or create custom merge function. Default applyOp handles standard LWW; only override if needed.

Step 13: Test cycle: (a) Run migrations in D1 (managed via wrangler). (b) Run db.foo.clear() in resetDb() in src/lib/dexie.ts if needed for test isolation. (c) Call generateOp({ entity_kind: 'foo', entity_id: 'test-123', op_type: 'create', payload: { field1: 'value' }, user_id: 'user-xyz' }). (d) Await applyLocalOp(op) to check Dexie table updated. (e) Await pushPullOnce({ userId: 'user-xyz' }) to sync to server. (f) Query D1 foo table to verify materialization.

Step 14: (Optional) Add POST /api/admin/backfill support: no code change needed if case added to materializeRow. The backfill route already loops all ops and calls materializeRow; if entity_kind FOO is recognized, it will materialize.

Step 15: (Optional) If entity has server-side cron jobs (like digest, recur, due-tasks), create src/app/api/cron/foo/route.ts querying foo table from D1. Follow pattern in src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts.

Step 16: Update TypeScript types: Run tsc or your build tool to verify no type errors. Dexie, Kysely, and Op types should all align. Check that applyLocalOp and materializeRow compile with new case branch.

Step 17: (Optional but recommended) Add test in tests/sync-integration.test.ts or new tests/foo-sync.test.ts: create op, apply locally, call pushPullOnce, query server D1, assert field_hlcs and data match expected LWW merge. Test idempotency by calling pushPullOnce twice.

dimensionMaps.dimension: Agents (Groq LLM Pipeline for Intent Routing & Extraction)

keyFiles.role: Core LLM client: exports makeGroqClient(apiKey), callGroqJSON<T>() with json_object response_format, withRetry() exponential backoff wrapper; defines GroqModel union = 'openai/gpt-oss-20b' | 'openai/gpt-oss-120b' | 'whisper-large-v3-turbo'
Intent classifier: routeIntent({client, text}) → RouterResponse; calls callGroqJSON with model gpt-oss-20b, temp=0, maxTokens=64; validates against RouterResponseSchema; returns {intent, confidence}
Zod enum INTENTS = ['log_money','log_task','query_money','query_task','chat']; RouterResponseSchema validates {intent: enum, confidence: 0-1}
System prompt builder ROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT; lists 5 intents with rules & examples; expects JSON {intent, confidence} only; tie-breaker logic for ambiguous inputs
Domain agent parseTaskEntry({client, text, nowIso?, userTz?}) → TaskAgentResponse; model gpt-oss-120b, temp=0, maxTokens=256; extracts {title, due_at (ISO UTC), priority (low/medium/high)}
Zod TaskAgentResponseSchema = {title: string[1-200], due_at: datetime | null, priority: enum[low/medium/high]}
System prompt builder buildTaskAgentSystemPrompt({nowIso, userTz}); rules for title extraction (strip 'remind me to'), due_at parsing (relative dates → UTC), priority cue detection; returns JSON-only

Domain agent parseMoneyEntry({client, text, categories, nowIso?, userTz?, defaultCurrency?}) → MoneyAgentResponse; model gpt-oss-120b; extracts {amount (int paise/cents), currency (ISO 4217), direction (out/in), category_name (exact match), description, occurred_at (ISO UTC)}
Zod MoneyAgentResponseSchema = {amount: int ≥0, currency: enum(SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES), direction: enum[out/in], category_name: string | null, description: string | null, occurred_at: datetime}

System prompt builder buildMoneyAgentSystemPrompt({categories, nowIso, userTz, defaultCurrency}); rules for amount conversion (rupees→paise, dollars→cents, lakhs, 'k' suffix, JPY no minor unit), direction cues (spent/paid→out, earned/got→in), category matching from active list, occurred_at timezone conversion

Query agent parseMoneyQuery({client, text, categories, nowIso?, userTz?}) → QueryMoneyResponse; model gpt-oss-120b; parses free-text query into structured search plan {direction, category_name, period: {from/to ISO UTC, label}}
Zod QueryMoneyResponseSchema = {direction: enum[out/in], category_name: string | null, period: {from: datetime, to: datetime, label: string}}

System prompt builder buildQueryMoneySystemPrompt({nowIso, userTz, categories}); rules for period extraction (this week→Mon-Mon, last month→calendar, last N days→rolling), direction inference, category exact matching (case-insensitive), label humanization

Vision agent parseReceiptImage({client, imageBase64, mime, categories, nowIso, userTz, defaultCurrency}) → MoneyAgentResponse & {source:'receipt'}; uses model llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct (fallback qwen3.6-27b); extracts merchant, amount, currency, date, category from image
Voice transcription groqWhisper({client, blob, filename}) → WhisperResult = {transcript, lang?, duration_ms?}; model whisper-large-v3-turbo, response_format='verbose_json', language='en'

Narrative generator writeDigestNarrative({client, metrics, weekLabel}) → string; model gpt-oss-120b, temp=0.3 (not deterministic like others); builds human financial summary from DigestMetrics; buildDigestSystemPrompt()/fallbackSummary() for fallback

Voice input handler: multipart/form-data audio → groqWhisper() → routeIntent() → conditional agent calls (log_money, log_task, query_money, else null) → SSE stream {step, payload, intent}; loads user prefs, categories from DB

Text input handler: JSON {text, categories} → routeIntent() → conditional agent calls → JSON {transcript, intent, confidence, payload}; same conditionals as voice route; no streaming; used by manual/text entry
SSE parser callVoiceApiStreaming(blob, onEvent) → VoiceFinalPayload | null; consumes /api/voice stream events {step, payload, transcript, error}; parses 'data: {json}' SSE format
Op-level schema TaskPayloadSchema = {title, due_at?, priority?, completed_at?, source: enum[voice/manual], raw_input?}; extends agent TaskAgentResponse with source tracking
Op-level schema MoneyPayloadSchema; extends agent response with op-specific fields; used in op_log for sync
Core type definitions: ENTITY_KINDS = [...'money','task','learning','note',...]; OpSchema validates {entity_kind, payload, entity_id, hlc}; defines entity_kind enum for all domain types
UI type ChipDraft = (MoneyPayload & {kind:'money',...}) | (TaskPayload & {kind:'task'}); maps agent payload to confirmation UI; defines what agent response becomes in UI

patterns: Every agent follows: (1) agent.ts exports async function parse*(args) returning typed response; (2) schemas/*.ts defines Zod schema for that agent's response; (3) prompts/*.ts exports buildSystemPrompt(context) returning string. All three are imported by the agent.ts file.

All agent functions take (client: Groq, text: string, ...context?) and call callGroqJSON<unknown>({client, model: string, system: string, user: text, temperature: 0, maxTokens: N}) wrapped in withRetry({attempts: 3, baseMs: 300-500}). Response is parsed via Zod.safeParse(); throws if invalid.

Router is entry point: routeIntent({client, text}) classifies utterance into INTENTS enum, returns {intent, confidence}. Then /api/agent or /api/voice branches on intent === 'log_money' | 'log_task' | 'query_money' etc., calling corresponding agent.

System prompts embed dynamic context: nowIso (ISO UTC current time), userTz (timezone string), categories (active list for matching), currency/lang hints. Prompts always end with 'Return ONLY this JSON object (no prose...)' + example shape. Temperature always 0 except digest (0.3).

Response schema validation: all agent responses must Zod.safeParse(raw).success === true. If false, throw error with parsed.error.message + raw JSON for debugging. Schema field types (int, enum, datetime, string) are strict.

Intent-to-domain mapping: 'log_money' → money domain → MoneyPayloadSchema → op_log kind:'money'; 'log_task' → task domain → TaskPayloadSchema → op_log kind:'task'. Each intent maps to exactly one domain and op kind.

Category/entity exact matching: money agent matches category_name against active categories array; if no match, sets to null (never invents). Query agent requires exact spelling or null. Case matching varies: money is case-sensitive by list, query is case-insensitive string comparison.

Timestamp handling: all due_at/occurred_at fields are ISO 8601 UTC strings. Agent prompts receive userTz and interpret relative times (tomorrow, last Tuesday) in that timezone, then convert to UTC. DB stores UTC; UI converts back to userTz on read.

Amount unit conversion: agents work in smallest currency units: INR 1 rupee = 100 paise (so ₹80 → 8000), USD $1 = 100 cents (so $5.50 → 550), JPY has no minor unit (so ¥1500 → 1500). MoneyPayloadSchema enforces amount: z.number().int().nonnegative().

Agent chaining: router → domain agent only. No agent calls another agent. Digest agent is async only (called from cron, not user input). Receipt vision is separate from voice pipeline; both map to MoneyPayloadSchema eventually.

Error messages include raw response for debugging: 'agent_name: invalid response — {validation error message}\nRaw: {JSON.stringify(raw)}'. Thrown errors bubble to API route and return {error: message, status: 502 or 400}.
User context loaded once per request: loadUserPrefs(db, userId) fetches primary_currency and tz; these are passed to all agents in that request. Prefs are per-user singleton in user_prefs table.
Response format mandatory: all callGroqJSON calls explicitly set response_format: {type: 'json_object'}. No streaming; each agent waits for full completion.

Model selection: router uses gpt-oss-20b (cheaper, faster, 64 token max); domain agents use gpt-oss-120b (reasoning, 256 token max); receipt vision uses llama-4-scout-17b-16e-instruct; whisper is dedicated audio model.
Intent confidence: router returns 0.0-1.0; /api/agent includes in response; used by UI for post-parsing review prompts. Voice route discards confidence (streaming; payload only).

Fall-through logic for unimplemented intents: if intent === 'query_task' | 'chat', return {transcript, intent, confidence, payload: null}. No agent runs; UI handles null payload (no confirmation chip created).
gotchas: Category name matching is case-sensitive in money agent but the prompt says to pick from 'active spend categories' list passed as JSON strings — user utterance 'Food' must exactly match list name 'Food', or result is null. Query agent uses case-insensitive comparison ('food' → 'Food' if same letters).

Amount is integer in smallest unit, never float. Groq may return 8000 or '8000' (string); MoneyAgentResponseSchema.amount = z.number().int() will coerce and fail on '8000.5'. Ensure prompt says 'integer in smallest unit'.

UTC conversion trap: prompts receive nowIso as ISO UTC and userTz as string like 'Asia/Kolkata'. Groq has NO timezone library — it can't actually convert. It's a reasoning problem. If prompt says 'tomorrow at 15:00 local → ISO UTC', you must verify with examples that Groq is doing math correctly (e.g., 'Asia/Kolkata is UTC+5:30, so 15:00 local is 09:30 UTC'). Hard-code examples in prompts.

Retry logic uses exponential backoff: baseMs * Math.pow(3, i). For baseMs=300, retries are 0ms, 300ms, 900ms. For baseMs=500, retries are 0ms, 500ms, 1500ms. Total wait ≈1.2s per agent. If Groq rate-limits (429), all 3 attempts fire sequentially.

JSON parse failure: if Groq returns 'I cannot process that' or partial JSON, JSON.parse() throws. Error message is 'groq: failed to parse JSON response'. No fallback; request fails entirely. Always catch and log the raw response.
Empty transcript from whisper: if Groq returns empty or whitespace-only transcript, groqWhisper() throws 'whisper: empty transcript'. Voice route will catch and SSE error event. No silent fallback.

Categories list is not validated by agent before use — if categories = [] (no active categories), money agent will receive spendList='(none)' in prompt and correctly return category_name: null. But if caller passes duplicate category names, agent has no guard; deduplication is caller's responsibility.

Router classification not perfect at low confidence: if router.confidence < 0.5 but returns an intent anyway, agent will run. UI should warn user on low confidence but won't reject. Tie-breaker rules in ROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT are best-effort heuristics.

Source field tracking: money agent response does NOT include source field. It's added by /api/agent or /api/voice routes ('voice' or 'manual'). Receipt agent hard-codes source: 'receipt'. If new agent doesn't get source injected by route, op will be missing source field and may fail validation.

Model migration risk: Groq deprecated llama-3.1-* in July 2026. Code now uses gpt-oss-20b/120b. If Groq deprecates these, all agents break silently (Groq returns 503 or 404, withRetry exhausts, error thrown). Monitor Groq status page or add fallback model logic.

Streaming response in /api/voice is fragile: if controller.enqueue() fails mid-stream, SSE parser sees incomplete JSON and warns but doesn't crash. Client may not receive final payload event. Server logs error but doesn't retry.

Digest agent uses temperature=0.3 (non-zero): fallback summary is hardcoded string, not agent call. If agent fails 3x or takes >10s, route should call fallbackSummary(metrics) instead. Check cron/digest route for this fallback.

Op schema version: each new domain agent must match op_log schema_version. If you add a new intent ('log_learning') but forget to bump op schema, op validation fails silently. Check /lib/op-schemas/index.ts getPayloadSchemaForKind(kind) switch statement.

Duplicate intent handling: if you add 'log_learning' to INTENTS enum but forget to add it to /api/agent route conditionals, intent will route correctly but then fall through to chat fallback (payload: null). Silent degradation; no error.

Voice route loads categories on every request: even for 'chat' or 'query_task' intents that don't need categories. Not a bug but inefficient; caller can't skip prefetch. For new domain that doesn't need categories, you'll pay the DB query anyway.

Confidence not returned in voice route: /api/voice only emits {intent, payload}; router.confidence is calculated but discarded. If you want user to see 'low confidence, confirm?', you must add confidence to SSE payload.

Receipt agent fallback model qwen/qwen3.6-27b: if primary vision model fails, code retries with fallback. But if both fail, error bubbles and no op created. Consider adding a manual fallback response (e.g., amount=0, category=null) for severe failures.

Retry attempts hardcoded: router uses 3 attempts with 300ms backoff; agents use 3 attempts with 500ms backoff; receipt agent uses 2 attempts with 800ms backoff. If you need longer backoff or more retries, you must edit each withRetry() call individually (no config).

Timezone ambiguity: 'this Friday' could mean in N days. Prompt rules say 'upcoming Friday'. If today IS Friday, does 'Friday' mean today or next week? Prompt is silent. Test edge cases with actual Groq calls.

Phone number in amount field: if user says 'my phone is 9876543210', money agent may parse it as amount=9876543210. Prompt says 'integer in smallest unit' but doesn't prevent noise. Router's low confidence for such inputs is your only guard.
